claims: Markdown plans are hard to review for visual people; the skill renders the plan as a UI
Each section gets thumbs up / thumbs down or comments; a copy button exports all feedback to paste back into Claude Code

Demo output: 'Hero with key stats (120K stars...)', '7 scrollable sections with fade-in', 'Implementation roadmap with all 1x tasks', 'HUD mockup showing the minimal UI', 'Review system on every section', arrow keys navigate sections
General advice: find friction in your workflow, make a skill for it, install it
how_to_steps: Have Claude Code write a detailed plan (demo plan lives under docs/superpowers/plans/)
Run /visualplanner; a background agent generates an interactive HTML breakdown and opens it in the browser
Walk the sections (arrow keys), thumbs up/down or comment on each
Press the copy button and paste the feedback into Claude Code; it now has all review notes

relevance.why: Plan review is the highest-leverage human step for a solo founder, and reviewing a rendered page with inline comments is faster and more accurate than scrolling markdown; the skill is free and tiny.

implement_score.why: Install ethanplusai/visualplanner as a Claude Code skill (minutes). Could be combined with the phased-plan gate so each phase page is approved before build. Risk: generating HTML for every plan costs tokens; use on large features only.
